react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a dominant steroid-hormone signal. RaMP multi-DB ORA (Reactome + SMPDB + KEGG + WikiPathways) returns Steroid biosynthesis (WP:WP496) as the top hit with FDR = 1.01e-15 and fold-enrichment = 2502, driven by five input steroids (dihydrotestosterone, androstenedione, estrone, testosterone, and dehydroepiandrosterone). The m/z-direct mummichog against the empirical human_mfn network independently recovers the same biological theme, ranking C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) at rank 0 (p = 3.36e-4) and Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) at rank 1 (p = 5.04e-4), together capturing 13 mummichog-identified steroid metabolites with perfect overlap with the five ORA hits. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA returns map hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) with the same five steroids mapped. The cross-paradigm winner is the steroid biosynthesis / androgen-and-estrogen-metabolism axis, spanning the RaMP namespace WP496, KEGG:map00150, SMPDB:SMP00068, and REACT:R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones). The non-steroid metabolites coumarin, spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, and doxycycline are flagged as pathway peripherals (coumarin maps to xenobiotics metabolism at rank 4 in mummichog; spironolactone is a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist that may intersect steroid metabolism as a xenobiotic effector). Dehydroepiandrosterone and testosterone serve as upstream substrates; androstenedione, estrone, and dihydrotestosterone are downstream products/intermediates, collectively implicating CYP17A1, CYP19A1 (aromatase), and HSD family enzymes as candidate effectors. No InChIKey conflicts were detected; all 10 compounds are structurally distinct and self-consistent.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-database ORA identified Steroid biosynthesis (WP:WP496, FDR=1.01e-15) and Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism across SMPDB and KEGG (SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150, FDR=2.95e-14), with the Reactome Metabolism of steroid hormones pathway also significant (REACT:R-HSA-196071, FDR=1.84e-13). Mummichog network analysis confirmed this signal at the top two ranks: C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM, p=4.2e-4) and Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (p=5.88e-4). MetaboAnalystR KEGG ORA independently mapped five input steroids to hsa00140. Five steroid metabolites are the drivers of this signal: dehydroepiandrosterone, androstenedione, testosterone, 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one, and estrone. Coumarin mapped only to xenobiotics metabolism in Mummichog and was not enriched in any ORA tool, indicating it is peripheral to the steroid signal.
